title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on Basic Medical Care and Health Promotion

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of developing medical and health care and health promotion, ensuring citizens' access to basic medical and health services, improving citizens' health levels, and advancing the building of a Healthy China.
Article 2 This Law shall apply to activities in medical and health care, health promotion, and the supervision and administration thereof.

Article 3 Medical and health care and health promotion undertakings shall adhere to a people-centered approach and serve the people's health.
Medical and health care undertakings shall adhere to the principle of public welfare.

Article 4 The State and society shall respect and protect citizens' right to health.
The State shall implement the Healthy China strategy, popularize healthy living, optimize health services, improve health security, build a healthy environment, develop the health industry, and enhance citizens' health levels throughout their entire life cycle.
The State shall establish a health education system to guarantee citizens' right to receive health education and improve their health literacy.

Article 5 Citizens shall have the right to obtain basic medical and health services from the State and society according to law.
The State shall establish a basic medical and health system, develop and improve the medical and health service system, and protect and realize citizens' right to obtain basic medical and health services.

Article 6 People's governments at all levels shall place the people's health in a strategic position of priority development, integrate health concepts into all policies, adhere to the principle of prevention first, improve the health promotion work system, organize and implement health promotion plans and actions, promote nationwide fitness, establish a health impact assessment system, and include improvements in key health indicators of citizens in the performance assessment of government target responsibilities.
The whole society shall jointly care for and support the development of medical and health care and health promotion undertakings.

Article 7 The State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall lead the work on medical and health care and health promotion.
The competent health department of the State Council shall be responsible for overall coordination of medical and health care and health promotion work nationwide. Other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for related medical and health care and health promotion work within their respective functions.
The competent health departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for overall coordination of medical and health care and health promotion work within their respective administrative regions. Other relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for related medical and health care and health promotion work within their respective functions.

Article 8 The State shall strengthen basic scientific research in medicine, encourage innovation in medical science and technology, support the development of clinical medicine, promote the transformation and application of medical scientific and technological achievements, advance the integrated development of medical and health care and information technology, promote appropriate medical and health technologies, and improve the quality of medical and health services.
The State shall develop medical education, improve the medical education system that meets the needs of the development of medical and health undertakings, and vigorously train medical and health personnel.

Article 9 The State shall vigorously develop traditional Chinese medicine undertakings, adhere to the principle of equal emphasis on Chinese and Western medicine and the combination of inheritance and innovation, and give play to the unique role of traditional Chinese medicine in medical and health care and health promotion undertakings.

Article 10 The State shall rationally plan and allocate medical and health resources, focus on the grassroots level, and take various measures to give priority to supporting the development of medical and health institutions at and below the county level, and improve their medical and health service capacity.

Article 11 The State shall increase financial input into medical and health care and health promotion undertakings, and provide key support through increased transfer payments and other means to develop medical and health care and health promotion undertakings in old revolutionary base areas, ethnic minority areas, border areas, and economically underdeveloped areas.

Article 12 The State shall encourage and support citizens, legal persons, and other organizations to participate in medical and health care and health promotion undertakings by lawfully establishing institutions and making donations or grants, so as to meet citizens' diverse, differentiated and personalized health needs.
Where citizens, legal persons, or other organizations donate property for medical and health care and health promotion undertakings, they shall enjoy tax preferences according to law.

Article 13 Organizations and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to medical and health care and health promotion undertakings shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with state regulations.

Article 14 The State shall encourage and support foreign exchanges and cooperation in the field of medical and health care and health promotion.
Activities of foreign exchanges and cooperation in medical and health care and health promotion shall comply with laws and regulations, and safeguard national sovereignty, security, and public interests.

Article 15 Basic medical and health services refer to services such as disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, nursing and rehabilitation provided with appropriate drugs, appropriate technologies, and appropriate equipment, which are necessary for maintaining human health, commensurate with the level of economic and social development, and fairly accessible to citizens.
Basic medical and health services include basic public health services and basic medical services. The State shall provide basic public health services free of charge.

Article 16 The State shall take measures to ensure that citizens enjoy safe and effective basic public health services, control risk factors affecting health, and improve the level of disease prevention and control.
The national basic public health service items shall be jointly determined by the competent health department of the State Council together with the finance department of the State Council, the competent department of traditional Chinese medicine, and others.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, on the basis of the national basic public health service items, supplement and determine basic public health service items for their respective administrative regions, and report them to the competent health department of the State Council for recordation.

Article 17 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may incorporate service contents targeting key areas, key diseases, and specific populations into basic public health service items and organize their implementation.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall carry out special prevention and control work for major diseases and major health risk factors within their respective administrative regions.

Article 18 People's governments at or above the county level shall provide basic public health services by establishing specialized public health institutions, grassroots medical and health institutions, and hospitals, or by purchasing services from other medical and health institutions.

Article 19 The State shall establish and improve the health emergency response system for emergencies, formulate and improve emergency plans, organize and carry out health emergency work such as medical treatment, epidemiological investigation and disposal, and psychological assistance for emergencies, so as to effectively control and eliminate hazards.

Article 20 The State shall establish a system for the prevention and control of infectious diseases, formulate and organize the implementation of plans for the prevention and treatment of infectious diseases, strengthen surveillance and early warning of infectious diseases, adhere to the principles of prevention first, combining prevention with treatment, joint prevention and control, mass prevention and control, source prevention and control, and comprehensive management, block transmission routes, protect susceptible populations, and reduce the harm of infectious diseases.
Any organization or individual shall accept and cooperate with measures taken by medical and health institutions according to law for the prevention, control, and elimination of the harm of infectious diseases, such as investigation, testing, sample collection, isolation treatment, and medical observation.

Article 21 The State shall implement a vaccination system and strengthen immunization program work. Residents shall have the right and obligation to receive immunization program vaccines according to law. The government shall provide immunization program vaccines to residents free of charge.

Article 22 The State shall establish a system for the prevention, control and management of chronic non-communicable diseases, carry out surveillance, investigation and comprehensive prevention and control interventions for chronic non-communicable diseases and their pathogenic risk factors, promptly identify high-risk populations, and provide services such as diagnosis and treatment, early intervention, follow-up management, and health education to patients and high-risk populations.

Article 23 The State shall strengthen occupational health protection. People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate plans for the prevention and treatment of occupational diseases, establish and improve the occupational health working mechanism, strengthen supervision and management of occupational health, and improve the comprehensive prevention and treatment capacity and level of occupational diseases.
Employers shall control occupational disease hazard factors, adopt comprehensive management measures such as engineering technology, personal protection, and health management, and improve the working environment and working conditions.

Article 24 The State shall develop maternal and child health care undertakings, establish and improve the maternal and child health service system, provide health care and common disease prevention and treatment services for women and children, and safeguard the health of women and children.
The State shall take measures to provide citizens with premarital health care, maternal health care, and other services, promote reproductive health, and prevent birth defects.

Article 25 The State shall develop health care undertakings for the elderly. The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall incorporate health management and common disease prevention for the elderly into basic public health service items.

Article 26 The State shall develop disability prevention and rehabilitation undertakings for persons with disabilities, improve the disability prevention and rehabilitation and security systems, and take measures to provide basic rehabilitation services for persons with disabilities.
People's governments at or above the county level shall give priority to the rehabilitation of children with disabilities and combine rehabilitation with education.

Article 27 The State shall establish and improve the pre-hospital emergency medical service system to provide timely, standardized, and effective emergency services for patients with acute and critical conditions.
The competent health departments, the Red Cross Society, and other relevant departments and organizations shall actively carry out first aid training, popularize first aid knowledge, and encourage medical and health personnel and persons trained in first aid to actively participate in first aid services in public places. Public places shall be equipped with necessary first aid equipment and facilities in accordance with regulations.
An emergency center (station) shall not refuse or delay providing emergency services to patients with acute and critical conditions on the ground of non-payment.

Article 28 The State shall develop mental health undertakings, build and improve the mental health service system, safeguard and enhance citizens' mental health, and prevent and treat mental disorders.
The State shall take measures to strengthen the mental health service system and personnel team building, promote the effective connection of mental health education, psychological assessment, psychological counseling, and psychotherapy services, set up psychological assistance hotlines providing public welfare services to the public, and strengthen mental health services for key populations such as minors, persons with disabilities, and the elderly.

Article 29 Basic medical services shall be mainly provided by medical and health institutions established by the government. Medical and health institutions established by social forces are encouraged to provide basic medical services.

Article 30 The State shall promote the implementation of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system for basic medical services, guide non-emergency patients to first seek medical treatment at grassroots medical and health institutions, implement a first-diagnosis responsibility system and a referral review responsibility system, and gradually establish a mechanism featuring first diagnosis at the grassroots level, two-way referral, separate treatment of acute and chronic diseases, and coordination between upper and lower levels, and link it with the basic medical insurance system.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the medical and health needs of their respective administrative regions, integrate government-established medical and health resources within the region, and establish coordinated medical service cooperation mechanisms such as medical alliances in light of local conditions. Medical and health institutions established by social forces are encouraged to participate in medical service cooperation mechanisms.

Article 31 The State shall promote the implementation of family doctor contract service by grassroots medical and health institutions, establish family doctor service teams, sign agreements with residents, and provide basic medical and health services based on residents' health conditions and medical needs.

Article 32 When receiving medical and health services, citizens shall have the right to informed consent according to law regarding matters such as the condition, diagnosis and treatment plan, medical risks, and medical expenses.
Where surgery, special examination, or special treatment is required, medical and health personnel shall promptly explain the medical risks, alternative treatment plans, and other information to the patient and obtain the patient's consent; where it is impossible or inappropriate to explain to the patient, they shall explain to the patient's close relatives and obtain their consent. If otherwise provided by law, such provisions shall prevail.
The conduct of clinical trials of drugs and medical devices and other medical research shall comply with medical ethics norms, pass ethical review according to law, and obtain informed consent.

Article 33 Citizens receiving medical and health services shall be respected. Medical and health institutions and medical and health personnel shall care for and treat patients equally, respect patients' human dignity, and protect patients' privacy.
Citizens receiving medical and health services shall comply with the diagnosis and treatment system and the order of medical and health services, and respect medical and health personnel.

Article 34 The State shall establish and improve a medical and health service system that covers both urban and rural areas, with complementary functions and continuous coordination, composed of grassroots medical and health institutions, hospitals, specialized public health institutions, and others.
The State shall strengthen the construction of county hospitals, township health centers, village clinics, community health service centers (stations), specialized public health institutions, and others, and establish and improve the rural medical and health service network and the urban community health service network.

Article 35 Grassroots medical and health institutions shall mainly provide basic medical and health services such as prevention, health care, health education, disease management, establishment of health records for residents, diagnosis and treatment of common and frequently-occurring diseases, rehabilitation and nursing for certain diseases, receiving patients transferred from hospitals, and referring patients beyond their service capacity to hospitals.
Hospitals shall mainly provide medical and health services such as disease diagnosis and treatment, especially diagnosis and treatment of acute, critical and complicated diseases, emergency medical treatment and rescue for emergencies, and health education, and carry out work such as medical education, training of medical and health personnel, medical scientific research, and professional guidance for grassroots medical and health institutions.
Specialized public health institutions shall mainly provide public health services such as prevention and control of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases, occupational diseases, endemic diseases, health education, maternal and child health care, mental health, pre-hospital emergency medical services, blood collection and supply, food safety risk monitoring and assessment, and prevention of birth defects.

Article 36 Medical and health institutions of various levels and types shall cooperate with division of labor to provide citizens with comprehensive and full-cycle medical and health services including prevention, health care, treatment, nursing, rehabilitation, and hospice care.
People's governments at all levels shall take measures to support medical and health institutions in establishing cooperation mechanisms with pension institutions, child welfare institutions, and community organizations to provide safe and convenient medical and health services for the elderly and orphaned and disabled children.

Article 37 People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate and implement plans for the medical and health service system, scientifically allocate medical and health resources, establish medical and health institutions, and provide guarantees for citizens to obtain basic medical and health services.
When the government establishes medical and health institutions, it shall take into account the population, economic and social development status, medical and health resources, health risk factors, incidence rate, prevalence rate, and emergency treatment needs of the administrative region.

Article 39 The State shall implement classified management of medical and health institutions.
The medical and health service system shall adhere to the principle of taking non-profit medical and health institutions as the main body and for-profit medical and health institutions as a supplement. The government shall establish non-profit medical and health institutions, play a leading role in basic medical and health undertakings, and ensure fair access to basic medical and health services.
Medical and health institutions established or participated in with government funds or donated assets shall not be established as for-profit medical and health institutions.
Medical and health institutions shall not lease or contract out medical departments. Non-profit medical and health institutions shall not distribute or distribute in disguised form profits to their contributors or founders.

Article 40 Medical and health institutions established by the government shall adhere to the nature of public welfare, incorporate all revenues and expenditures into budget management, and rationally set up and control their scale in accordance with the plan for the medical and health service system.
The State shall encourage medical and health institutions established by the government to cooperate with social forces in establishing non-profit medical and health institutions.
Medical and health institutions established by the government shall not invest with other organizations to set up medical and health institutions without independent legal person status, nor shall they cooperate with social capital to establish for-profit medical and health institutions.

Article 41 The State shall take various measures to encourage and guide social forces to lawfully establish medical and health institutions, and support and regulate the cooperation between medical and health institutions established by social forces and those established by the government in various types of medical services, discipline construction, personnel training, etc.
Medical and health institutions established by social forces shall enjoy the same rights as medical and health institutions established by the government in terms of designation as basic medical insurance providers, key specialty construction, scientific research and teaching, grade evaluation, access to specific medical technologies, and professional title evaluation for medical and health personnel.
Social forces may choose to establish non-profit or for-profit medical and health institutions. Non-profit medical and health institutions established by social forces shall, in accordance with regulations, enjoy the same policies as medical and health institutions established by the government regarding taxation, financial subsidies, land use, water, electricity, gas, and heat use, and shall accept supervision and management according to law.

Article 42 The State shall, on the basis of established medical and health institutions, rationally plan and set up national medical centers and national and provincial regional medical centers to diagnose and treat difficult and critical diseases, research and overcome major medical problems, and cultivate high-level medical and health personnel.

Article 43 Medical and health institutions shall comply with laws, regulations, and rules, establish and improve internal quality management and control systems, and be responsible for the quality of medical and health services.
Medical and health institutions shall, in accordance with clinical diagnosis and treatment guidelines, clinical technical operation specifications, industry standards, and medical ethics norms, carry out reasonable examinations, medication, and diagnosis and treatment, strengthen prevention of medical and health safety risks, optimize service processes, and continuously improve the quality of medical and health services.

Article 44 The State shall implement classified management of the clinical application of medical and health technologies, and exercise strict management over medical and health technologies that are technically difficult, involve high medical risks, or require high service capability and professional skill levels.
Medical and health institutions conducting clinical application of medical and health technologies shall be commensurate with their functions and tasks, follow the principles of science, safety, standardization, effectiveness, and economy, and conform to ethics.

Article 45 The State shall establish a modern hospital management system with clear powers and responsibilities, scientific management, sound governance, efficient operation, and strong supervision.
Hospitals shall formulate articles of association, establish and improve their corporate governance structure, and improve their medical and health service capacity and operational efficiency.
Article 46 The practice site of a medical and health institution is a public place for providing medical and health services. No organization or individual shall disrupt its order.

Article 47 The State shall improve the medical risk sharing mechanism, encourage medical institutions to participate in medical liability insurance or establish medical risk funds, and encourage patients to participate in medical accident insurance.

Article 48 The State shall encourage medical and health institutions to continuously improve technologies, equipment, and services for prevention, health care, diagnosis, treatment, nursing, and rehabilitation, and support the development of medical and health technologies suitable for application in grassroots and remote areas.

Article 49 The State shall promote nationwide health informatization, promote the application and development of health and medical big data, artificial intelligence, etc., accelerate the construction of medical and health information infrastructure, formulate technical standards for the collection, storage, analysis and application of health and medical data, and use information technology to promote the popularization and sharing of high-quality medical and health resources.
People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall take measures to promote the application of information technology in medical and health fields and medical education, and support the exploration and development of new models and new forms of medical and health services.
The State shall take measures to promote medical and health institutions in establishing and improving medical and health information exchange and information security systems, apply information technology to carry out telemedicine services, and build an integrated online and offline medical service model.

Article 50 When emergencies such as natural disasters, accident disasters, public health incidents, and social security incidents seriously threaten the life and health of the people occur, medical and health institutions and medical and health personnel shall obey the dispatch of government departments and participate in health emergency response and medical treatment. Personnel who become ill, disabled, or die as a result of participation shall be given work-related injury benefits or pensions, martyr commendations, and other related treatment in accordance with regulations.

Article 51 Medical and health personnel shall promote the lofty professional spirit of revering life, saving the injured and healing the wounded, being willing to contribute, and boundless love, abide by industry norms, adhere to medical ethics, and strive to improve professional level and service quality.
Medical and health industry organizations, medical and health institutions, and medical schools shall strengthen education on medical ethics and professional conduct for medical and health personnel.

Article 52 The State shall formulate plans for the training of medical and health personnel, establish a training mechanism and a supply-demand balance mechanism that adapt to industry characteristics and social needs, improve the system of medical school education, postgraduate education, and continuing education, establish and improve standardized training systems for resident physicians and specialist physicians, and build a medical and health workforce of appropriate scale, reasonable structure, and balanced distribution.
The State shall strengthen the training and use of general practitioners. General practitioners shall mainly provide services such as diagnosis and treatment of common and frequently-occurring diseases, referral, prevention, health care, rehabilitation, as well as chronic disease management and health management.

Article 53 The State shall implement a practice registration system for medical and health personnel such as physicians and nurses according to law. Medical and health personnel shall obtain corresponding professional qualifications according to law.

Article 54 Medical and health personnel shall follow the laws of medical science, comply with relevant clinical diagnosis and treatment technical specifications, various operational norms, and medical ethics norms, use appropriate technologies and drugs, conduct reasonable diagnosis and treatment, treat patients according to their conditions, and shall not implement excessive medical treatment on patients.
Medical and health personnel shall not use their positions to demand or illegally accept property or seek other improper benefits.

Article 55 The State shall establish and improve personnel, remuneration, and reward systems that conform to the characteristics of the medical and health industry, reflecting the professional characteristics and technical labor value of medical and health personnel.
Appropriate allowances shall be given to medical and health personnel engaged in infectious disease prevention and control, radiology, mental health, and other special positions in accordance with national regulations. Allowance standards shall be adjusted periodically.

Article 56 The State shall establish a system for medical and health personnel to regularly engage in medical and health work at the grassroots level and in difficult and remote areas.
The State shall take measures such as targeted free training, paired assistance, and re-employment after retirement to strengthen the construction of the medical and health workforce at the grassroots level and in difficult and remote areas.
Practicing physicians who are promoted to deputy senior technical titles shall have accumulated more than one year of experience in providing medical and health services at medical and health institutions below the county level or through paired assistance.
Preferential treatment shall be given to medical and health personnel working at the grassroots level and in difficult and remote areas in terms of salary allowances, title evaluation, career development, education and training, and commendation and awards.
The State shall strengthen the construction of the rural medical and health workforce, establish a career development mechanism that connects counties, townships, and villages, and improve the multi-channel subsidy mechanism for service income and the pension policy for rural medical and health personnel.

Article 57 The whole society shall care for and respect medical and health personnel, maintain a good and safe order for medical and health services, and jointly build a harmonious doctor-patient relationship.
The personal safety and human dignity of medical and health personnel shall not be violated, and their lawful rights and interests shall be protected by law. No organization or individual shall threaten or endanger the personal safety of medical and health personnel, or infringe upon their human dignity.
The State shall take measures to ensure the practice environment for medical and health personnel.
Article 58 The State shall improve the drug supply guarantee system, establish a work coordination mechanism, and ensure the safety, effectiveness, and accessibility of drugs.

Article 59 The State shall implement the essential drug system, select an appropriate number of essential drug varieties to meet the basic drug needs for disease prevention and treatment.
The State shall publish the essential drug list, and dynamically adjust it based on drug clinical application practices, drug standard changes, new drug marketing status, etc.
Essential drugs shall be prioritized for inclusion in the basic medical insurance drug list according to regulations.
The State shall improve the supply capacity of essential drugs, strengthen quality supervision of essential drugs, and ensure fair accessibility and rational use of essential drugs.

Article 60 The State shall establish and improve a drug review and approval system guided by clinical needs, support the development and production of clinically urgently needed drugs, pediatric drugs, and drugs for the prevention and treatment of rare diseases, major diseases, etc., to meet the needs of disease prevention and treatment.

Article 61 The State shall establish and improve a whole-process traceability system for drug research, development, production, distribution, and use, strengthen drug management, and ensure drug quality.

Article 62 The State shall establish and improve a drug price monitoring system, conduct cost-price investigations, strengthen drug price supervision and inspection, and investigate and deal with illegal acts such as price monopoly, price fraud, and unfair competition according to law to maintain drug price order.
The State shall strengthen the management and guidance of drug classification procurement. Bidders participating in drug procurement bidding shall not bid with quotes below cost, nor bid by means of fraud, bid rigging, abuse of market dominance, etc.
Article 63 The State shall establish central and local two-level pharmaceutical reserves to meet emergency needs such as major disasters, epidemics, and other emergencies.

Article 64 The State shall establish and improve a drug supply monitoring system, collect, summarize and analyze drug supply information in a timely manner, and regularly publish information on drug production, distribution, and use.

Article 65 The State shall strengthen the management of medical devices, improve standards and specifications for medical devices, and improve the safety and effectiveness of medical devices.
The health administrative department of the State Council and the health administrative departments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, based on the advanced nature, suitability, and accessibility of technology, formulate allocation plans for large medical equipment, and promote reasonable allocation and full sharing of medical equipment within the region.

Article 66 The State shall strengthen the protection and development of traditional Chinese medicine, fully reflect the characteristics and advantages of traditional Chinese medicine, and play its role in prevention, health care, medical treatment, and rehabilitation.

Article 67 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen health education work and its professional talent training, establish a system for the release of core information on health knowledge and skills, popularize health science knowledge, and provide scientific and accurate health information to the public.
Medical and health, education, sports, propaganda, and other institutions, grassroots autonomous organizations, and social organizations shall carry out the publicity and popularization of health knowledge. Medical and health personnel, when providing medical and health services, shall carry out health education for patients. News media shall carry out public service publicity of health knowledge. The publicity of health knowledge shall be scientific and accurate.

Article 68 The State shall incorporate health education into the national education system. Schools shall use various forms to implement health education, popularize health knowledge, scientific fitness knowledge, first aid knowledge and skills, improve students' awareness of active disease prevention, cultivate students' good hygienic habits and healthy behavior habits, and reduce and improve students' adverse health conditions such as myopia and obesity.
Schools shall offer physical education and health courses according to regulations, and organize students to carry out activities such as broadcast exercises, eye exercises, and physical exercise.
Schools shall be equipped with school doctors according to regulations, and establish and improve health rooms, health care rooms, etc.
The education administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, according to regulations, incorporate students' physical health levels into the school assessment system.

Article 69 Citizens are the first responsible persons for their own health, establish and practice the health management concept of being responsible for their own health, actively learn health knowledge, improve health literacy, and strengthen health management. Family members shall be encouraged to care for each other and form healthy lifestyles that suit their own and family characteristics.
Citizens shall respect the health rights and interests of others, and shall not harm the health of others or social public interests.

Article 70 The State shall organize surveys and statistics on the health status of residents, carry out physical fitness monitoring, evaluate health performance, and formulate and improve health-related laws, regulations, policies, and plans based on the evaluation results.

Article 71 The State shall establish a system for monitoring, investigating, and risk assessing diseases and health risk factors. People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall organize research on health risk factors and formulate comprehensive prevention and control measures for major issues affecting health.
The State shall strengthen the prevention and control of environmental issues affecting health, organize research on the impact of environmental quality on health, and take measures to prevent and control diseases related to environmental issues.

Article 72 The State shall vigorously carry out the patriotic health campaign, encourage and support mass health and health activities such as Patriotic Health Month, rely on and mobilize the masses to control and eliminate health risk factors, improve environmental sanitation, and build healthy cities, healthy towns, and healthy communities.
Article 73 The State shall establish a scientific and strict food and drinking water safety supervision and management system to improve safety levels.

Article 74 The State shall establish a nutrition status monitoring system, implement nutrition intervention plans for economically underdeveloped areas and key populations, carry out nutrition improvement actions for minors and the elderly, advocate healthy eating habits, and reduce the risk of diseases caused by unhealthy diets.

Article 75 The State shall develop the national fitness cause, improve the public fitness service system covering urban and rural areas, strengthen the construction of public sports facilities, organize and support national fitness activities, strengthen national fitness guidance services, and popularize scientific fitness knowledge and methods.
The State shall encourage the opening of sports venues and facilities of units to the public.

Article 76 The State shall formulate and implement health work plans for minors, women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, and strengthen health services for key populations.
The State shall promote long-term care security work and encourage the development of long-term care insurance.

Article 77 The State shall improve the public place sanitation management system. Health administrative departments and other relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen health supervision of public places. Public place health supervision information shall be disclosed to the public according to law.
Public place business units shall establish and improve and strictly implement health management systems to ensure that their business activities continuously meet the national health requirements for public places.

Article 78 The State shall take measures to reduce the harm of smoking to citizens' health.
Smoking control in public places shall be strengthened, and supervision and enforcement shall be intensified.
Tobacco product packaging shall be printed with warnings explaining the hazards of smoking.
It shall be prohibited to sell tobacco and alcohol to minors.

Article 79 Employers shall create a healthy environment and conditions for employees, strictly implement labor safety and health and other relevant regulations, actively organize employees to carry out fitness activities, and protect employees' health.
The State shall encourage employers to carry out employee health guidance work.
The State shall advocate that employers conduct regular health check-ups for employees. Where laws and regulations have provisions on health check-ups, such provisions shall apply.

Article 80 People's governments at all levels shall earnestly fulfill their responsibilities for developing medical and health and health promotion undertakings, establish an investment mechanism for medical and health and health promotion undertakings that is compatible with economic and social development, fiscal conditions, and health indicators, include medical and health and health promotion funds in their government budgets, and use them mainly to ensure basic medical services, public health services, basic medical security, and the construction, operation, and development of government-run medical and health institutions according to regulations.

Article 81 People's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the supervision and management of funds through budgets, audits, supervision and enforcement, social supervision, and other means.

Article 82 The costs of basic medical services shall be mainly paid by the basic medical insurance fund and individuals. The State shall raise basic medical insurance funds through multiple channels according to law, and gradually improve the sustainable financing and benefit level adjustment mechanism for basic medical insurance.
Citizens have the right and obligation to participate in basic medical insurance according to law. Employers and employees shall pay basic medical insurance premiums for employees in accordance with national regulations. Urban and rural residents shall pay basic medical insurance premiums for urban and rural residents in accordance with regulations.

Article 83 The State shall establish a multi-level medical security system with basic medical insurance as the main body, supplemented by commercial health insurance, medical assistance, employee mutual medical care, and medical charity services.
The State shall encourage the development of commercial health insurance to meet the diverse health protection needs of the people.
The State shall improve the medical assistance system to ensure that eligible people in need obtain basic medical services.

Article 84 The State shall establish and improve a negotiation mechanism between basic medical insurance agencies and designated medical and health institutions under agreement, scientifically and reasonably determine the payment standards and methods of the basic medical insurance fund, guide medical and health institutions to provide reasonable diagnosis and treatment, promote orderly flow of patients, and improve the efficiency of the use of the basic medical insurance fund.

Article 85 The scope of payment of the basic medical insurance fund shall be formulated by the national medical security administrative department of the State Council and shall hear the opinions of the health administrative department, traditional Chinese medicine administrative department, drug supervision and management department, finance department, etc. of the State Council.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in accordance with relevant national regulations, supplement and determine specific items and standards for payment within their administrative regions from the basic medical insurance fund, and report to the national medical security administrative department of the State Council for record.
The national medical security administrative department of the State Council shall organize evidence-based medical and economic evaluations of the basic medical insurance drug list, diagnosis and treatment items, medical service facility standards, etc. included in the payment scope, and shall hear opinions from relevant parties such as the health administrative department, traditional Chinese medicine administrative department, drug supervision and management department, and finance department of the State Council. The evaluation results shall serve as the basis for adjusting the payment scope of the basic medical insurance fund.

Article 86 The State shall establish and improve a comprehensive medical and health supervision and management system that combines institutional self-governance, industry self-discipline, government supervision, and social supervision.
The health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall implement localized and whole-industry supervision and management of the medical and health industry.

Article 87 The medical security administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall improve the capacity and level of medical security supervision, strengthen supervision and management of medical service behaviors and medical expenses included in the payment scope of the basic medical insurance fund, and ensure rational use, safety, and controllability of the basic medical insurance fund.

Article 88 People's governments at or above the county level shall organize the health, medical security, drug supervision and management, development and reform, finance, and other departments to establish a communication and consultation mechanism, strengthen institutional connection and work coordination, and improve the efficiency and guarantee level of medical and health resource use.

Article 89 People's governments at or above the county level shall regularly report on the work of basic medical and health and health promotion to the people's congress at the corresponding level or its standing committee, and accept supervision according to law.

Article 90 Where the relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level fail to fulfill their duties related to medical and health and health promotion work, the people's government at the same level or the relevant department of the people's government at the higher level shall interview their principal responsible persons.
Where a local people's government fails to fulfill its duties related to medical and health and health promotion work, the people's government at the higher level shall interview its principal responsible person.
The interviewed departments and local people's governments shall immediately take corrective measures.
The interview situation and rectification situation shall be included in the work evaluation and assessment records of relevant departments and local people's governments.

Article 91 The health administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a performance evaluation system for medical and health institutions, organize evaluations of the service quality, medical technology, drug and medical equipment use of medical and health institutions. Evaluations shall absorb the participation of industry organizations and the public. The evaluation results shall be disclosed to the public in an appropriate manner and serve as an important basis for evaluating medical and health institutions and health supervision.

Article 92 The State shall protect citizens' personal health information and ensure the security of citizens' personal health information. No organization or individual shall illegally collect, use, process, or transmit citizens' personal health information, or illegally buy, sell, provide, or disclose citizens' personal health information.

Article 93 The health administrative departments and medical security administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a credit record system for medical and health institutions, personnel, etc., include it in the national credit information sharing platform, and implement joint punishments in accordance with national regulations.

Article 94 The health administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level and their entrusted health supervision institutions shall carry out medical and health and other administrative enforcement work within their administrative regions according to law.

Article 95 The health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall actively cultivate medical and health industry organizations, give play to their role in medical and health and health promotion work, and support their participation in the formulation of industry management norms, technical standards, and medical and health evaluation, assessment, and review work.
Article 96 The State shall establish a mechanism for the prevention and handling of medical disputes, properly handle medical disputes, and maintain medical order.

Article 97 The State shall encourage citizens, legal persons, and other organizations to carry out social supervision over medical and health and health promotion work.
Any organization or individual shall have the right to complain and report to the health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level and other relevant departments about acts violating the provisions of this Law.

Article 98 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, local people's governments at all levels, health administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level, and other relevant departments abuse their powers, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain, the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 99 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person practices without obtaining a medical institution practice license, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order cessation of practice activities, confiscate illegal gains and drugs and medical devices, and impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than twenty times the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than 10,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 10,000 yuan.
Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person forges, alters, buys, sells, leases, or lends a medical institution practice license, the health administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction, confiscate illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than fifteen times the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than 10,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the medical institution practice license shall be revoked.

Article 101 Where, in violation of this Law, a medical and health institution fails to have a sound medical information security system or safeguard measures, thereby causing the leakage of medical information, or fails to have a sound medical quality management and medical technology management system or safety measures, the competent department of health and health of the people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections, give a warning, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the said department may order the suspension of relevant practice activities, and shall investigate the legal liability of the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons according to law.

Article 103 Where, in violation of this Law, a bidder participating in a bid for drug procurement bids at a price lower than the cost, or bids by means of fraud, collusive bidding, abuse of a dominant market position, or other means, the competent department of medical security of the people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and confiscate its illegal gains; if the bid is won, the award of the bid shall be null and void, and a fine of not less than five per thousand but not more than ten per thousand of the amount of the winning project shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than five percent but not more than ten percent of the amount of the fine imposed on the entity shall be imposed on the legal representative, the principal responsible person, the directly responsible person in charge, and other liable persons; if the circumstances are serious, the bidder's qualification to participate in bids for drug procurement shall be disqualified for a period of two to five years and such disqualification shall be announced.

Article 104 Where, in violation of this Law, a person obtains basic medical insurance benefits by means of fraud, falsification of supporting materials, or other means, or a basic medical insurance agency, medical institution, drug business unit, or other entity defrauds expenditures from the basic medical insurance fund by means of fraud, falsification of supporting materials, or other means, the competent department of medical security of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose an administrative penalty in accordance with the provisions of the laws and administrative regulations on social insurance.

Article 105 Where, in violation of this Law, a person disrupts the order of the practice premises of a medical and health institution, threatens or endangers the personal safety of medical and health personnel, infringes upon the personal dignity of medical and health personnel, illegally collects, uses, processes, or transmits citizens' personal health information, illegally buys, sells, provides, or discloses citizens' personal health information, or commits any other act, which constitutes a violation of public security administration, the person shall be given a public security administration penalty according to law.

Article 106 Where a violation of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if personal injury or property damage is caused, civil liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 107 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms have the meanings specified:
(1) "Main health indicators" means the average life expectancy, maternal mortality rate, infant mortality rate, under-five mortality rate, and the like.
(2) "Medical and health institutions" means primary medical and health institutions, hospitals, specialized public health institutions, and the like.
(3) "Primary medical and health institutions" means township health centers, community health service centers (stations), village clinics, infirmaries, outpatient departments, clinics, and the like.
(4) "Specialized public health institutions" means centers for disease control and prevention, specialized disease prevention and treatment institutions, health education institutions, emergency centers (stations), blood stations, and the like.
(5) "Medical and health personnel" means practicing physicians, practicing assistant physicians, registered nurses, pharmacists (dispensers), laboratory technicians (assistants), imaging technicians (assistants), village doctors, and other health professionals.
(6) "Essential drugs" means drugs that meet the basic drug needs for disease prevention and treatment, are suitable for the current basic national conditions and guarantee capacity, have appropriate dosage forms, reasonable prices, ensured supply, and are fairly accessible.

Article 108 The provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities divided into districts and autonomous prefectures may, in light of local conditions, formulate specific measures for the development of medical and health and health undertakings in their respective localities.

Article 109 The State Council and the Central Military Commission shall, in accordance with this Law, formulate administrative measures for the medical and health and health promotion work of the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force.
Article 110 This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2020.
